source_caption:
Brittany Murphy and Eminem in ‘8 Mile’ (2002) 

8 Mile (2002) is a hip-hop drama starring Eminem as Jimmy “B-Rabbit” Smith Jr., a young white rapper trying to launch a career in 1995 Detroit, a city deeply divided by racial and socioeconomic lines along 8 Mile Road. The film follows his personal struggle, covering a crucial week of his life as he navigates a tumultuous relationship with his mother, a dead-end job, and the intense, often hostile local underground rap scene.

source_details.synopsis: 8 Mile is a 2002 American drama film produced and directed by Curtis Hanson from a script written by Scott Silver. It stars Eminem in his feature film debut, alongside Kim Basinger, Brittany Murphy, and Mekhi Phifer. Containing autobiographical elements from Eminem's life, the film follows Detroit rapper Jimmy Smith Jr., also known as B-Rabbit, as he attempts to launch a career in hip-hop, a music genre dominated by African Americans.
